name: Strategic Education Inc
business: Runs Strayer and Capella online universities, Australian and New Zealand institutions, and Sophia Learning courses for working adults and employer partners.

CEO appointment (context only, far outside window); CFO Daniel Jackson also long tenured (on calls since at least 2021)

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found in Baba corpus for 2026; the operative 'notional model' dates from the 2023 Investor Day (doc 145875).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Adjusted operating (EBIT) margin. Rate frame: 200 bps of expansion a year in the 2023 'notional model' (five-year basis), which the CEO tied explicitly to 2026 and 2027 on 2026-07-29. Plus a dollar program: upwards of $100M of operating expense savings by end of 2027, partly reinvested. Street comparison uses VA consensus operating margin (FY2025 VA 15.47% matches reported adjusted 15.5%). Calendar fiscal year, VA FY = company FY. first_stated is null: the 200 bps notional model was set at the 2023 Investor Day, whose exact date is not in the fetched sources. A $13M Australia FWO labor reserve hit Q2 2026; CEO said 200 bps is achievable 'potentially even including' it.

statements.quote: As I also just said, I'm more than confident in the 200 basis point EBIT margin expansion over this year, next year. That's how I think about the notional model relative to both 2026 and 2027.

statements.quote: I'm very confident that we will outperform the notional model's 200 basis points of EBIT margin expansion, potentially even including the $13 million FWO charge. If you exclude it, most definitely we would.

street.gap_assumption: consensus_ebitda_margin_by_fy = VA consensus EBITDA / revenue (same basis as data_comps ebitda_margin; VA broker EBITDA margin line differs slightly). Operating margin basis throughout, VA FY = calendar fiscal year. Target FY2027 = FY2025 VA operating margin 15.47% + 200 bps x 2 = 19.47% vs FY2027 consensus 18.35% = +111.7 bps. FY2026: 17.47% vs consensus 16.84% = +63.1 bps (part of the FY2026 gap may be the $13M FWO reserve, about 100 bps of revenue, if brokers include it). FY2028 consensus 19.66%. Only 3 brokers.
street.source: Baba data_financials fundamentals consensus (Visible Alpha), cid 1000926. Uplift = 111.7 bps x FY2027 revenue $1,338.5M / FY2027 consensus EBITDA $326.4M = 4.6%, flat D&A (data_compute).

evidence_of_progress.note: Operating margin basis. Q1 2026 (VA 1QFY-2026 actual) 14.12% vs 13.74% = +37.8 bps. Q2 2026 VA row still holds consensus; reported revenue $330M (+3%) and adjusted EPS $1.76 (+16%) with a $13M FWO reserve, margin YoY not computed. Q4 2025 operating margin +390 bps to 16.9%; FY2025 +260 bps to 15.5% (CEO, doc 145875). Revenue growth is below the 4% to 6% model on Australia visa caps and US enrollment declines. 4-month forward EBITDA revision +1.1%, 12-month +0.6%. Net cash, no debt.

verdict: Mechanically scores well (cheap, 200 bps a year through 2027 and about 112 bps above FY2027 consensus) but no management catalyst: a 13-year CEO restating a 2023 model, so it lacks the GXO change-of-hands trigger.
open_questions: Is the 112 bps FY2027 gap real or an artifact of only 3 brokers and how they treat the $13M FWO reserve and reinvested savings?
Does revenue (Australia visa caps, US unaffiliated enrollment declines) fall far enough below the 4% to 6% model to cap the margin path?
Will the board refresh management or hold a new Investor Day, since the notional model dates from 2023 and there is no new leadership?
